neighbours.label: a noun for the rate or period of a repeating motion or signal (frequency, beats, stride, tempo, clock cycle)
fire: The metronome was set so the band played at about a hundred beats per minute.
Long-distance runners often shorten their stride when they climb a steep hill.
The processor's clock cycle limits how fast each instruction can finish.
The radio signal has a frequency of about ninety megahertz in this region.
The coach asked the swimmers to raise their kicking tempo in the last lap.
Midwives measure how long the contractions last and the interval between them.
The pendulum swings with a period of almost exactly two seconds.
The drummer kept a steady rhythm while the singer improvised over the top.
quiet: The band played a long set and the crowd stayed until midnight.
Long-distance runners often slow down when they climb a steep hill.
The processor's cache size limits how much data it can hold close by.
The radio station has a large audience of farmers in this region.
The coach asked the swimmers to keep their heads down in the last lap.
Midwives measure the mother's blood pressure and check the baby's position.
The pendulum hangs from a brass hook above the old clock face.
The drummer sat at the back while the singer improvised over the top.

notes: card: beats, frequency, stride, tempo, clock; logit effect suppresses cycle/rhythm/repetition/pacing.
